transcript: Safe House is probably one of the more polarizing pieces I've seen in recent memory. Some might call it cutting-edge and brilliant, others might call it nonsensical and confusing. Needless to say, it's experimental. It's more or less a song cycle about the main and only character Grace and how she makes sense or survival out of her fragmented and traumatic memories. The scenes are presented in a nonlinear fashion, and even if you pay really close attention, I don't think you're meant to have a complete understanding of Grace's story. I would describe the music as primarily pensive underscoring or spooky techno songs sung by Grace. As far as my thoughts, I was impressed by Kate Gilmore's unsettling performance and I found Grace a really interesting character. Otherwise, I felt like I spent much of the show trying to put things together so I didn't really feel anything, but I was engaged or at least intrigued the entire time. I think if you're open to something that requires that level of engagement or you like experimental pieces that demand dissection and interpretation, this is for you. Safe House is running just through this weekend at St Ann’s Warehouse. With that, another program for my collection.
